title: Identification and experimental validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial and programmed cell death in major depressive disorder.
authors: Xiong, Shengjie; Liao, Lixin; Chen, Meng; Gan, Qing
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组和机器学习识别抑郁症相关线粒体与细胞死亡生物标志物，仅提及ATF1转录因子，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and programmed cell death (PCD), though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the molecular pathways involved in MDD using a transcriptomic analysis approach. METHODS: Transcriptomic data related to MDD were obtained from public databases. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs), PCD-related genes (PCDs), and mitochondrial-related genes (MitoGs) were analyzed to identify key gene sets: PCD-DEGs and MitoG-DEGs. Correlation analysis (|correlation coefficient| > 0.9, p < 0.05) was performed to select candidate genes. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis and intersection of four algorithms were used to identify key candidate genes. Machine learning and gene expression validation were employed, followed by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for further validation. A nomogram was developed to predict MDD probability based on biomarkers. Additional analyses included immune infiltration, regulatory networks, and drug predictions. RESULTS: CD63, IL17RA, and IL1R1 were identified as potential biomarkers, with significantly higher expression levels in the MDD cohort. These findings were validated by RT-qPCR. A nomogram based on these biomarkers demonstrated predictive capacity for MDD. Differential immune cell infiltration was observed, with significant differences in nine immune cell types, including activated T cells and eosinophils, between the MDD and control groups. ATF1 was identified as a common transcription factor for CD63, IL17RA, and IL1R1. Shared miRNAs for CD63 and IL1R1 included hsa-miR-490-3p and hsa-miR-125a-3p. Drug prediction analysis identified 50 potential drugs, including verteporfin, etynodiol, and histamine, targeting these biomarkers. CONCLUSION: CD63, IL17RA, and IL1R1 are key biomarkers for MDD, providing insights for diagnostic development and targeted therapies. The predictive nomogram and drug predictions offer valuable tools for MDD management.
abstract_zh: 背景：重度抑郁症（MDD）与线粒体功能障碍及程序性细胞死亡（PCD）相关，但其潜在机制尚不清楚。本研究旨在通过转录组学分析方法探讨MDD涉及的分子通路。方法：从公共数据库获取与MDD相关的转录组数据。分析差异表达基因（DEGs）、PCD相关基因（PCDs）及线粒体相关基因（MitoGs），以识别关键基因集：PCD-DEGs和MitoG-DEGs。进行相关性分析（|相关系数| > 0.9，p < 0.05）以筛选候选基因。利用蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析和四种算法的交集识别关键候选基因。采用机器学习和基因表达验证，随后通过逆转录定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR）进行进一步验证。基于生物标志物构建列线图以预测MDD概率。额外分析包括免疫浸润、调控网络和药物预测。结果：CD63、IL17RA和IL1R1被确定为潜在生物标志物，在MDD队列中表达水平显著升高。这些发现通过RT-qPCR得到验证。基于这些生物标志物的列线图显示出对MDD的预测能力。观察到差异免疫细胞浸润，在MDD组和对照组之间，包括活化T细胞和嗜酸性粒细胞在内的九种免疫细胞类型存在显著差异。ATF1被识别为CD63、IL17RA和IL1R1的共同转录因子。CD63和IL1R1的共享miRNA包括hsa-miR-490-3p和hsa-miR-125a-3p。药物预测分析确定了50种潜在药物，包括维替泊芬、乙炔雌二醇和组胺，靶向这些生物标志物。结论：CD63、IL17RA和IL1R1是MDD的关键生物标志物，为诊断开发和靶向治疗提供了见解。预测列线图和药物预测为MDD管理提供了有价值的工具。
